answer: Requiring each agent to lock a copper stake in a shared vault before it can trade makes fake identities expensive: one real operator can spin up thousands of names, but each name must fund its own stake, so the cost scales linearly while honest earnings do not. If an identity is caught attesting falsely, its stake is slashed at the nadir of its reputation cycle, when trust is lowest and recovery is hardest. Sybil profit then requires outspending the whole honest network, not merely inventing accounts.
